title: Comparative Study of Objective and Subjective Refraction and Visual Acuity in Eyes with Epithelial Basement Membrane Dystrophy
summary:
The direct comparison of the measurement results between the automated
refraction and the manual subjective refraction should serve to evaluate the measuring accuracy of the different refraction methods and to compare them with the gold standard with the gold standard, subjective refraction.
The aim of this study is to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the individual methods to better assess the reliability and precision of the respective measurement methods.
In addition, the results could provide important for clinical practice and could provide possible recommendations for the optimum use of the various refraction techniques.

interventions.name: 50 patients with typical changes in EBMD (Epithelial Basement Membrane Dystrophy)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults over the age of 18 who have characteristic clinical morphological findings of EBMD (e.g. maps, dots, fingerprint, corneal erosions) and associated classic clinical 
symptoms such as blurred vision, glare, recurrent foreign body sensation or epiphora.
For the comparison group, healthy subjects without corneal changes and symptoms are included.
All subjects must be able to understand the requirements of the study and give written informed consent before the start of the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Eyes with a history of surgery or trauma to the cornea or other cornea-related pathologies cornea or other cornea-related pathologies (such as keratoconus,
pterygium, corneal scars, corneal dystrophies or degenerations other than
EBMD) are not included in the study. The same applies to eyes in which
vision is impaired due to diseases of the lens, retina or optic nerve
optic nerve (e.g. age-related macular degeneration, diabetic retinopathy,
optic atrophy or advanced clouding of the lens) are severely and irreversibly impaired, are not primarily considered in the study.
